11.​Add after paragraph 30 and renumber (Edinburgh Southwest) 
 
Food inflation in particular is likely to cut into the British working class’s living 
standards in the next period, forcing thousands more into hunger and poverty. Britain 
imports 40% of all food and the majority of fruit, seafood, and about half of 
vegetables, another aspect of its reliance on the world economy. Its vulnerability was 
demonstrated at the onset of the Ukraine war, when shocks to fertiliser, energy and 
grain affected UK food inflation more than any other G7 country. The Iran war may 
have an even more dramatic effect on world food production, which will emerge as 
shocks to fertiliser and petrochemicals work their way through supply chains. Added 
to this is climate change, which has already been having a serious impact on both 
global and domestic agriculture. Last spring’s drought, the worst for 132 years, 
brought many regions of the country dangerously close to failed harvests. As extreme 
weather events increase and seasonal patterns become less predictable, food 
security will be further eroded. The resulting inflation and potential scarcity will have 
an enormous impact on consciousness, affecting every worker in the country. 
 
CC recommendation: Accept 
 
12.​Amend paragraph 31 (Preston Ribble) 
 
The crisis of capitalism reflects itself acutely in Britain in a sense of social decay. The very 
fabric of society seems to be falling apart. This fuels concerns not only about migration, but 
also about the rise of petty crime such as shoplifting and theft, which demagogues like 
Farage cynically tap into, exaggerate, and link to one another, as part of their rhetoric about 
‘broken Britain’. Starmer’s Labour and the Tories are no different, also banging the drum 
about ‘law and order’. The crisis within the British state – including overflowing prisons, 
backlogged courts, and a demoralised, scandal-ridden police force – only adds to the 
general sense of chaos and disorder, however. 
 
CC recommendation: Reject 
 
13.​Add after paragraph 33 and renumber (Edinburgh Central) 
 
This divisive rhetoric is not confined to migration, however, but also finds expression 
in the culture wars around questions of gender, including through the spread of the 
‘manosphere’ and rising transphobia. Studies show significant numbers of young 
boys expressing sympathy for misogynistic ideas, as alienation, combined with the 
absence of any genuine answer from the left, pushes a layer towards reactionary 
ideas. 
 
CC recommendation: Reject
